To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the magnetic and structural phase transitions in Co-doped 122 materials can be tuned by changing the size of the unit cell in a dimensionally controlled way.

the increased dimension of the Sr122 crystal structure relative to the Ba122 structure results in a single, first-order-like magnetic-structural transition, in contrast to the quasicontinuously-split magnetic and structural transitions in the higher dimensional Ba122 system.
the magnetic and structural phase transitions in Co-doped Ba(Fe$_x$Co$_{1-x})_2$As$_{2}$ (Co-doped 122) are split, and the splitting is a function of the dimensionality of the system.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the interplay between superconductivity, magnetism, and structural transitions in iron-based superconductors.
the study of the electronic properties of the iron-based superconductors.
the electronic and magnetic properties of iron-based superconductors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the magnetic and structural transition in the Co-doped Sr(Fe$_2$As$_{2})_1-x$(P,As)$_x$ are continuous, while in Co-doped Ba(Fe$_2$(As,P)$_2$) they are split into two transitions, and that the splitting is related to the relative size (magnitude) of superconducting temperature.
the dimensionality of the system is the most important factor in determining the magnetic and structural phase diagram.
Co-doping of Ba122 results in a splitting of magnetic and structural transitions and the superconductivity is not enhanced by this splitting.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the dimensionality of the system is a key factor for understanding the magnetic, structural, and superconducting phase transitions in these iron-based superconductors.

the superconducting temperature of the Co-doped Sr(Fe$_1-x$Co$_x$)As$_2$ system is much higher than that of the Co-doping Ba122 system, and the magnetic and structural transition temperatures in Co-doped Sr1212 are much closer to each other, than that in the Co-doping counterpart Ba122.
the superconductivity in the Co-doped Sr(Fe$_1-x$Co$_x$)2As2 (x=0.03) is not suppressed by the first order structural transition at Tc=20K.
The main takeaway from our work is that

a dimensionality-driven splitting of the magnetic and structural phase transitions in Co-doped 122 compounds can be used as a probe of the relative superconducting transition temperatures in these compounds.
the magnetic and structural degrees of freedom are strongly coupled in the iron-based superconductors, and that the dimensionality of a material plays an important role in this coupling.
the dimensionally tuned splitting of magnetic and structural transitions in the Co-doped Ba/Sr122 superconductors is a result of the relative size of the superconducting temperatures.
